The weather in Spain and in Romania
It’s a very hot July day in Madrid. Ana and Mihai are sitting in the shade.
Phew, it’s so hot! How many degrees is it today?
It’s thirty-eight degrees. In July and August it’s always very hot in Madrid.
I’m really hot. And in winter? Is it cold?
Yes, it’s cold, but not very. It almost never snows in Madrid.
What’s the weather like in Romania?
In summer it’s hot too, but in winter it’s very cold.
In January it’s minus ten and it snows a lot in the mountains.
Minus ten! How cold! And in spring?
Spring is very nice, but it rains quite a lot. I always carry an umbrella.
My favourite season is autumn. It’s neither cold nor hot.
Mine is winter: I love snow.
So, shall we go to the mountains in December? It snows there.
Perfect! But right now… shall we go to the pool?
The LL in “llueve” is read like “y”: llueve = “yweh-beh”.
Verano, invierno, nieve, llueve: all with a soft “b”. Don’t pronounce an English “v”!
In English we say “it’s hot”, “it’s cold”. In Spanish you literally say “it makes heat”: HACE + noun.
For rain and snow there are special verbs. And for the sky you use ESTAR:
The typical mistake: “Es calor” or “Está calor”. Correct: “Hace calor”.
The months look a lot like English, but they are written with a small letter:
“In July” = en julio. “In spring” (when?) = en primavera.
The Spanish and English months share the same Latin names. Only “enero” (January) looks quite different.
3. The date: el cinco de mayo
The formula is simple: el + number + de + month. For the first day you can also say “el primero”.
Today is the fifth of May.
My birthday is on the twentieth of October.
Years are read as whole numbers, not in pairs as in English: 2026 = dos mil veintiséis (“two thousand twenty-six”).
Both mean “very / a lot”, but they are not interchangeable:
mucho calor (very hot, literally “a lot of heat”)
Because “calor” is a noun, you say “hace MUCHO calor”, never “hace muy calor”.
“Mucho” agrees when it comes before a noun: mucho calor, mucha lluvia, muchos días, muchas personas.
5. Hot: HACE calor, TENGO calor or ESTÁ caliente?

The same with cold: hace frío (outside), tengo frío (I’m cold), la sopa está fría (the soup is cold).
Don’t say “estoy caliente” to mean you feel hot: in Spanish it has a rather… inappropriate meaning. Say “tengo calor”!

What the weather is like in different parts of Spain throughout the year.
Spain is a big country, and the weather is very different in each region.
In the north, in Galicia and Asturias, it rains a lot all year round.
That’s why the landscape is very green. The summers aren’t very hot.
In the south, in Andalusia, it’s almost always sunny.
In July and August, in Seville or Córdoba, it’s over forty degrees.
Many people have a siesta after lunch because it’s too hot.
In the centre, in Madrid, winters are cold and dry, and summers are very hot.
On the Mediterranean coast, in Valencia or Barcelona, the climate is mild.
In winter the temperature is usually between ten and fifteen degrees.
In the mountains, for example in the Pyrenees or the Sierra Nevada, it snows in winter.
Many people go skiing there from December to March.
And in the Canary Islands the weather is nice all year round: it’s eternal spring!

It almost never snows in Madrid. Winter is cold, but it’s usually sunny and the sky is blue.
But today, on the eighth of January, something incredible happens. Ana gets up, looks out of the window and shouts: “Snow!”.
The streets, the cars and the trees are white. There’s almost fifty centimetres of snow.
There’s no metro, there are no buses, and the schools are closed. Ana can’t go to work.
She calls Mihai. “Are you awake? Look out of the window!”.
Mihai laughs: “Ana, I’m Romanian. For me, this is normal!”.
An hour later, they are both in Retiro Park. There are lots of people: children with sledges, families, dogs running through the snow.
Mihai teaches Ana how to make a snowman, like in Romania.
They give it a red scarf and a carrot for a nose.
After two hours they are very cold. Ana’s hands are red and she has no gloves.
They go to a café and have a hot chocolate with churros.
“I love snow,” says Ana. “But I prefer summer.”
“Not me,” answers Mihai. “Winter is my favourite season. And today Madrid looks like Brașov!”.
The next day the snow began to melt. But the snowman in the Retiro stayed there for three more days.
